trait_layer: visible flower colour; anthocyanin-based red/blue-purple proxy
environment_axis: warmth index; rainfall; UV-B; temperature range; precipitation seasonality
source_result: red proportion negatively associated with warmth index and positively with UV-B after regional/phylogenetic correction; northwest and Tibetan Plateau enriched in red/blue-purple
inference_limit: community/grid composition; pigment chemistry inferred from colour class; does not establish trait-before-niche causality

source_result: among UV-patterned taxa, larger UV-absorbing petal area at higher altitude and lower temperature; OU fit better than BM
inference_limit: UV floral pigmentation is not equivalent to visible anthocyanin redness; abiotic association not proof of range expansion causality

source_result: subalpine assemblage had significantly greater floral colour diversity; several high-elevation lineages showed greater absolute/rate of colour evolution
inference_limit: does not isolate anthocyanin chemistry and authors did not attribute pattern specifically to abiotic stress

source_result: high-altitude floras are phylogenetically clustered; colour hue/contrast show weak phylogenetic signal and patterns are interpreted mainly through bee-colour preferences rather than a simple abiotic pigmentation gradient
inference_limit: community assembly study; does not test anthocyanin chemistry or trait-before-niche order

system: Erythranthe + Diplacus radiations; plus two polymorphic species
source_result: within polymorphic species anthocyanin frequency tracks abiotic stress, including higher elevation/lower temperature in D. mephiticus; across radiations no phylogenetically corrected joint evolution of flower colour and environmental affinity
inference_limit: critical counterexample: micro environmental association need not scale to macroevolutionary coupling

source_result: white reconstructed as ancestral visible state; yellow restricted to putative ancestral SW China/N Vietnam while red/white have wider distributions
inference_limit: no species-level climatic niche model in source; raw tree unavailable locally; geographic expansion is not yet linked causally to pigmentation

environment_axis: warm coastal versus snow-rich Japan; current/LGM climatic niches
source_result: C. rusticana occupies snow-rich colder habitat and shows long-term ecological differentiation, yet its petals are slightly lighter than C. japonica (P<0.01; 89.3% colour-space overlap); both remain red-flowered
inference_limit: close-pair evidence argues against simple floral redness/anthocyanin amount as the enabling cold-adaptation trait; pigment composition, leaves and pollinator syndrome may still coevolve

system: Theaceae phylogenomics with Camellia diversification shift
source_result: a significant Camellia diversification-rate shift coincides with the Mid-Miocene Climatic Optimum in the time-calibrated nuclear phylogeny
inference_limit: temporal coincidence is not evidence that warm climate caused diversification; this constrains but does not test flower-pigment niche causality
